decisions.choice: "không xem bề ngoài của người ta" (L); "không thiên vị theo địa vị" (B); "không ưu đãi ai vì địa vị" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek idiom is "does not receive a face" (m4). Literal keeps the picture of outward appearance; Balanced and Readable say it plainly, with no gender span, since "người ta" includes everyone.

decisions.choice: Deus não recebe [a] face de {{gender:uma pessoa|um homem}}
alternatives: Deus não faz acepção de pessoas
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew idiom (m4), as the English Literal does, with the gender setting on the noun Portuguese has to choose. "Não faz acepção de pessoas", the traditional church phrase, is no longer understood.

decisions.choice: deram ... a mão direita, em sinal de comunhão
decisions.reason: Portuguese "mão direita de comunhão" is not a phrase a reader would understand; "em sinal de" says that the handshake sealed a partnership (m10). Readable says "apertaram a mão ... como sinal de que éramos parceiros".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans in Amharic
alternatives: capitalised pronouns, as the English alternative has them
decisions.reason: The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting for capitalised pronouns has nothing to change; pronouns for God and for Christ are written plainly through the letter.

decisions.choice: የሰውን ፊት (a person's face), with no gender span
alternatives: a span such as the English {{gender:a person|a man}}
decisions.reason: "ሰው" already means a human being, man or woman, so Amharic has no second wording for the setting to offer.

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun spans; honorific forms for God ("उन्होंने", "वे ... कार्य कर रहे थे")
decisions.reason: Devanagari has no capital letters, so the English deity_pronoun setting has nothing to change in Hindi. Respect for God comes from the honorific third person at every level (style guide, sections 4 and 7). The same through this chapter.

decisions.choice: "परमेश्वर मनुष्य का मुँह नहीं देखते", with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender span on "a person". "मनुष्य" is already inclusive in Hindi, so there is nothing for the setting to change. "मुँह देखना" is also a living Hindi idiom for favouring someone by their standing (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "ख़तनारहितों", "ख़तनावालों" (L); "ख़तनारहितों", "ख़तना किए हुओं" (B); "ग़ैर-यहूदी लोगों", "यहूदियों" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans: Literal and Balanced keep the picture of circumcision, Readable names the two peoples (meaning decision m7).

decisions.choice: "केफ़ा" (L, B); "पतरस" (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:18: Literal and Balanced keep the name Paul uses here, Readable the name readers know (meaning decision m9). Paul calls him "पतरस" himself in verses 7-8.

decisions.choice: "संगति का दाहिना हाथ दिया" (L, B); "साथी मानकर ... हाथ मिलाया" (R)
decisions.reason: The right hand of fellowship sealed a partnership (meaning decision m10); Readable says so with the everyday handshake.

decisions.choice: человека, without a gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender setting on "a person|a man"; Russian "человек" already means any human being, so no setting is needed.

decisions.choice: Кифа (L, B); Пётр (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:18: Literal and Balanced keep the name Paul uses, Readable the name readers know.

decisions.choice: the broken opening and the two asides set off with "――" (L, B); separate sentences (R)
alternatives: round brackets, as the English Literal
decisions.reason: Japanese marks an aside with "――"; round brackets in Japanese read as an editor's note. The sentence that breaks off at "from those who seemed" is picked up again by "added nothing" (m1).

decisions.choice: "人" with no gender span; "割礼の[者]" / "無割礼の[者]" (L), "割礼を受けた人々" / "割礼を受けていない人々" (B), "ユダヤ人" / "ユダヤ人でない人々" (R)
alternatives: a gender span on "人", as the English Literal
decisions.reason: "人" already includes men and women, so the English span is not needed. The two peoples (m7) are named as in Romans 3:30: by the rite at Literal and Balanced, by who they are at Readable.

decisions.choice: обличчя людини (no gender span)
decisions.reason: Ukrainian "людина" is already inclusive, so the English span has no counterpart.

source.text: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν, ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι.

records.literal_gloss: Only the poor that we should remember, which also I was eager this very thing to do.

en.L: Only [they asked] that we should remember the poor, the very thing that I also was eager to do.
en.B: They asked only that we keep remembering the poor, and that is the very thing I was eager to do.
en.R: They asked only one thing: that we would keep on helping the poor. That was something I was already eager to do.

es.L: Solo [pidieron] que nos acordáramos de los pobres, precisamente lo que yo también me esforcé por hacer.
es.B: Solo nos pidieron que siguiéramos acordándonos de los pobres, y eso es justamente lo que yo estaba deseoso de hacer.
es.R: Nos pidieron una sola cosa: que siguiéramos ayudando a los pobres. Eso era algo que yo ya deseaba mucho hacer.

sw.L: Ila [waliomba] tu kwamba tuwakumbuke maskini, jambo lile lile ambalo mimi pia nilijitahidi kulifanya.
sw.B: Waliomba tu kwamba tuendelee kuwakumbuka maskini, nalo ndilo jambo nililokuwa na hamu kubwa ya kulifanya.
sw.R: Waliomba jambo moja tu: kwamba tuendelee kuwasaidia maskini. Hilo nilikuwa tayari na hamu kubwa ya kulifanya.

fr.L: Seulement, [ils nous ont demandé] de nous souvenir des pauvres, ce que justement je me suis empressé de faire.
fr.B: Ils nous ont seulement demandé de continuer à nous souvenir des pauvres, et c’est précisément ce que j’avais à cœur de faire.
fr.R: Ils ne nous ont demandé qu’une seule chose : continuer à aider les pauvres. Et c’est une chose que je tenais déjà beaucoup à faire.

ko.L: 다만 [그들은] 우리가 가난한 사람들을 기억하기를 [부탁했고], 그것은 나도 바로 힘써 해 오던 일이었습니다.
ko.B: 그들은 다만 우리가 가난한 사람들을 계속 기억해 달라고 부탁했는데, 그것은 바로 내가 힘써 해 오던 일이었습니다.
ko.R: 그들이 부탁한 것은 한 가지뿐이었습니다. 우리가 가난한 사람들을 계속 도와 달라는 것이었습니다. 그것은 내가 이미 열심히 하고 싶어 하던 일이었습니다.

vi.L: Chỉ [họ xin] chúng tôi nhớ đến những người nghèo, là điều chính tôi cũng đã sốt sắng làm.
vi.B: Họ chỉ xin chúng tôi tiếp tục nhớ đến những người nghèo, và đó chính là điều tôi vẫn hăng hái làm.
vi.R: Họ chỉ xin một điều: chúng tôi hãy tiếp tục giúp đỡ người nghèo. Đó là điều tôi vốn đã hăng hái làm rồi.

pt.L: Somente [pediram] que nos lembrássemos dos pobres, aquilo mesmo que eu também me empenhei em fazer.
pt.B: Pediram apenas que continuássemos a nos lembrar dos pobres, e era justamente isso o que eu me empenhava em fazer.
pt.R: Eles pediram só uma coisa: que continuássemos ajudando os pobres. E isso era algo que eu já queria muito fazer.

am.L: ድሆችን እንድናስብ ብቻ [ለመኑን]፤ ይህንኑም እኔ ደግሞ ለማድረግ ተጋሁ።
am.B: የለመኑን ድሆችን ዘወትር እንድናስብ ብቻ ነው፤ እኔም ይህንኑ ለማድረግ ተግቼ ነበር።
am.R: የለመኑን አንድ ነገር ብቻ ነው፤ ድሆችን መርዳታችንን እንድንቀጥል ነው። ይህን ለማድረግ ቀድሞውንም እጓጓ ነበር።

hi.L: केवल [उन्होंने यह कहा] कि हम कंगालों को स्मरण रखें, और इसी काम को करने के लिए मैं भी उत्सुक था।
hi.B: उन्होंने केवल यह कहा कि हम ग़रीबों को याद रखते रहें, और यही काम करने के लिए मैं भी उत्सुक था।
hi.R: उन्होंने केवल एक बात माँगी: कि हम ग़रीबों की मदद करते रहें। यह काम करने के लिए मैं पहले से ही उत्सुक था।

ru.L: Только [просили], чтобы мы помнили о бедных, что я и старался сделать.
ru.B: Они просили только, чтобы мы продолжали помнить о бедных, и именно это я и старался делать.
ru.R: Они попросили лишь об одном: чтобы мы продолжали помогать бедным. Я и сам очень хотел это делать.

ja.L: ただ、わたしたちが貧しい人々を覚えているように[と、彼らは求めました]。まさにそのことを、わたしも熱心に行ってきました。
ja.B: 彼らが求めたのはただ一つ、わたしたちが貧しい人々のことを忘れないようにということでした。それこそ、わたしも熱心に努めてきたことです。
ja.R: その人たちがわたしたちに頼んだのは、一つだけでした。貧しい人たちを助け続けてほしい、ということです。それは、わたしが前からぜひしたいと思っていたことでした。

uk.L: Тільки [просили], щоб ми памʼятали про бідних, що я й старався саме це робити.
uk.B: Вони попросили тільки, щоб ми й далі памʼятали про бідних, і саме це я й прагнув робити.
uk.R: Вони попросили тільки одного: щоб ми й далі допомагали бідним. Я й сам дуже хотів це робити.

decisions.choice: the only request the leaders added to the agreement of verse 9
alternatives: a separate request made at another time
decisions.reason: μόνον ("only") with ἵνα ("that") continues the agreement of verse 9: the one thing asked of Paul and Barnabas. It is not a condition on the gospel, which the leaders had already accepted, but a request about care for the needy.

decisions.choice: remember the poor: keep giving practical help to poor believers, especially in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: To "remember" the poor means to act for them, and the present tense says to keep doing it. Paul later gathered money from his Gentile churches "for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem" (Romans 15:26; 1 Corinthians 16:1-3). The Jerusalem believers are most likely meant, though the words could cover the poor more widely.

decisions.choice: Paul was eager to do this, and did it
alternatives: Paul became eager only after this meeting
decisions.reason: ἐσπούδασα is a past tense meaning "I was eager, I made every effort". It may look back to help he had already carried (Acts 11:29-30) or forward to the collection he later organized. Either way, Paul shows that he gladly agreed.

decisions.choice: [they asked] (L); They asked (B, R)
alternatives: Only that we should remember the poor
decisions.reason: The Greek leaves out the verb; English needs one to make a sentence (m1).

decisions.choice: keep on helping
decisions.reason: Readable says what "remember" means here (m2).

source.text: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην, ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν·

records.literal_gloss: When but came Cephas to Antioch, to face to him I opposed, because condemned he was;

en.L: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to [his] face, because he stood condemned.
en.B: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him face to face, because he was clearly in the wrong.
en.R: When Peter came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he was plainly wrong.

es.L: Pero cuando Cefas vino a Antioquía, me opuse a él cara a cara, porque estaba condenado.
es.B: Pero cuando Cefas llegó a Antioquía, me enfrenté a él cara a cara, porque estaba claramente en falta.
es.R: Cuando Pedro llegó a Antioquía, me opuse a él abiertamente, cara a cara, porque era evidente que estaba equivocado.

sw.L: Lakini Kefa alipokuja Antiokia, nilimpinga uso kwa uso, kwa sababu alikuwa amehukumiwa.
sw.B: Lakini Kefa alipofika Antiokia, nilimpinga ana kwa ana, kwa sababu alikuwa amekosea waziwazi.
sw.R: Petro alipofika Antiokia, nilimpinga ana kwa ana, kwa sababu alikuwa amekosea wazi kabisa.

fr.L: Mais quand Céphas est venu à Antioche, je lui ai résisté en face, parce qu’il était condamné.
fr.B: Mais quand Céphas est venu à Antioche, je lui ai tenu tête en face, parce qu’il était manifestement dans son tort.
fr.R: Quand Pierre est venu à Antioche, je me suis opposé à lui ouvertement, parce qu’il avait clairement tort.

ko.L: 그러나 게바가 안디옥에 왔을 때, 나는 그를 얼굴을 맞대고 반대했습니다. 그가 책망받을 [잘못이] 있었기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 그러나 게바가 안디옥에 왔을 때, 나는 그와 얼굴을 맞대고 맞섰습니다. 그가 분명히 잘못했기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 베드로가 안디옥에 왔을 때, 나는 그 앞에서 대놓고 그에게 반대했습니다. 그가 분명히 잘못했기 때문입니다.

vi.L: Nhưng khi Sê-pha đến An-ti-ốt, tôi đã chống lại ông trước mặt, vì ông đáng bị lên án.
vi.B: Nhưng khi Sê-pha đến An-ti-ốt, tôi đã chống lại ông ngay trước mặt, vì rõ ràng ông đã sai.
vi.R: Khi Phi-e-rơ đến An-ti-ốt, tôi đã chống lại ông ngay trước mặt, vì rõ ràng ông đã sai.

pt.L: Mas, quando Cefas veio a Antioquia, eu me opus a ele face a face, porque ele estava condenado.
pt.B: Mas, quando Cefas veio a Antioquia, eu me opus a ele frente a frente, porque ele estava claramente errado.
pt.R: Quando Pedro veio a Antioquia, eu me opus a ele cara a cara, porque ele estava claramente errado.

am.L: ኬፋ ግን ወደ አንጾኪያ በመጣ ጊዜ፣ የተፈረደበት ስለ ነበር ፊት ለፊት ተቃወምኩት።
am.B: ኬፋ ግን ወደ አንጾኪያ በመጣ ጊዜ፣ ስሕተቱ ግልጽ ስለ ነበር ፊት ለፊት ተቃወምኩት።
am.R: ጴጥሮስ ወደ አንጾኪያ በመጣ ጊዜ፣ ስሕተት መሥራቱ ግልጽ ስለ ነበር ፊት ለፊት ተቃወምኩት።

hi.L: पर जब केफ़ा अन्ताकिया में आया, तो मैंने उसके मुँह पर उसका विरोध किया, क्योंकि वह दोषी ठहर चुका था।
hi.B: पर जब केफ़ा अन्ताकिया आया, तो मैंने आमने-सामने उसका विरोध किया, क्योंकि वह साफ़ ग़लती पर था।
hi.R: जब पतरस अन्ताकिया आया, तो मैंने उसके सामने ही उसका विरोध किया, क्योंकि वह साफ़-साफ़ ग़लत था।

ru.L: Когда же Кифа пришёл в Антиохию, я воспротивился ему в лицо, потому что он был осуждён.
ru.B: Но когда Кифа пришёл в Антиохию, я выступил против него лицом к лицу, потому что он был явно неправ.
ru.R: Когда Пётр пришёл в Антиохию, я открыто выступил против него, потому что он был явно неправ.

ja.L: しかし、ケファがアンティオキアに来たとき、わたしは面と向かって彼に反対しました。彼は責められるべき者となっていたからです。
ja.B: ところが、ケファがアンティオキアに来たとき、わたしは面と向かって彼に反対しました。彼は明らかにまちがっていたからです。
ja.R: ペトロがアンティオキアに来たとき、わたしはペトロに面と向かって反対しました。ペトロのしていることが、はっきりまちがっていたからです。

uk.L: А коли Кифа прийшов до Антіохії, я противився йому в обличчя, бо він був осуджений.
uk.B: Але коли Кифа прийшов до Антіохії, я виступив проти нього віч-на-віч, бо він був явно неправий.
uk.R: Коли Петро прийшов до Антіохії, я виступив проти нього просто в очі, бо він був явно неправий.

decisions.choice: Antioch in Syria, where Jewish and Gentile believers belonged to one church
decisions.reason: Antioch, the capital of the Roman province of Syria, had a church of Jews and Gentiles; it was the base from which Barnabas and Paul were sent out (Acts 11:19-26; 13:1-3).

decisions.choice: a new episode; whether it came after the meeting of verses 1-10 is not certain
decisions.reason: Ὅτε δὲ ("but when") turns to a new event. It most naturally follows the meeting just described, which would make Peter's conduct the more striking, but Paul may be arranging his account by subject rather than by date.

decisions.choice: he stood condemned: his own conduct showed he was in the wrong
alternatives: he had been condemned by others
decisions.reason: κατεγνωσμένος is a perfect participle of the verb "to condemn": he was in a state of being condemned. Verses 12-14 show by what: his own actions, which went against what he believed. Paul is not reporting a verdict passed by others.

decisions.choice: Cephas (L, B); Peter (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9: Readable uses the name readers know.

decisions.choice: clearly in the wrong (B); plainly wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Condemned" alone could suggest a court's sentence; Balanced and Readable say what Paul means (m3).

decisions.choice: "안디옥"
decisions.reason: The established Protestant Korean form of the name.

source.text: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν· ὅτε δὲ ἦλθον, ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν, φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς.

records.literal_gloss: Before the for to come some from James with the Gentiles he was eating; when but they came, he was drawing back and separating himself, fearing those of circumcision.

en.L: For before some [people] came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles; but when they came, he began drawing back and separating himself, fearing those of [the] circumcision.
en.B: Before some people came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But once they had come, he started to pull back and hold himself apart, afraid of those who insisted on circumcision.
en.R: Before some people came from James, Peter used to eat with the Gentile believers. But after they came, he began to pull away and no longer ate with them. He was afraid of the people who insisted that Gentile believers be circumcised.

es.L: Porque antes de que llegaran algunos de parte de Santiago, comía con los gentiles; pero cuando llegaron, se fue retirando y apartándose, temiendo a los de [la] circuncisión.
es.B: Antes de que llegaran algunos de parte de Santiago, solía comer con los gentiles. Pero una vez que llegaron, comenzó a retraerse y a mantenerse aparte, por miedo a los que insistían en la circuncisión.
es.R: Antes de que llegaran algunas personas de parte de Santiago, Pedro solía comer con los creyentes gentiles. Pero cuando ellos llegaron, empezó a alejarse y dejó de comer con ellos. Tenía miedo de los que insistían en que los creyentes gentiles debían circuncidarse.

sw.L: Kwa maana kabla ya kuja kwa [watu] fulani kutoka kwa Yakobo, alikuwa akila pamoja na watu wa mataifa; lakini walipokuja, akaanza kurudi nyuma na kujitenga, akiwaogopa wale wa tohara.
sw.B: Kabla watu fulani kutoka kwa Yakobo hawajafika, alikuwa na desturi ya kula pamoja na watu wa mataifa. Lakini walipofika, alianza kujiondoa na kujitenga nao, akiwaogopa wale waliosisitiza tohara.
sw.R: Kabla watu fulani kutoka kwa Yakobo hawajafika, Petro alikuwa akila pamoja na waumini wa mataifa. Lakini walipofika, alianza kujiondoa, akaacha kula pamoja nao. Aliwaogopa watu waliosisitiza kwamba waumini wa mataifa lazima watahiriwe.

fr.L: Car avant que certains viennent de chez Jacques, il mangeait avec les nations ; mais quand ils sont venus, il a commencé à se retirer et à se tenir à l’écart, par crainte de ceux de la circoncision.
fr.B: Avant l’arrivée de certaines personnes venues de chez Jacques, il mangeait avec les non-Juifs. Mais une fois qu’elles sont arrivées, il a commencé à se dérober et à se tenir à part, par peur de ceux qui exigeaient la circoncision.
fr.R: Avant que certaines personnes arrivent de chez Jacques, Pierre mangeait avec les croyants non juifs. Mais après leur arrivée, il a commencé à s’éloigner, et il ne mangeait plus avec eux. Il avait peur des gens qui voulaient obliger les croyants non juifs à se faire circoncire.

ko.L: 야고보에게서 어떤 [사람들]이 오기 전에는 그가 이방 사람들과 함께 먹곤 하였는데, 그들이 오자 할례[받은 사람들]을 두려워하여 물러나 자기를 따로 떼어 놓기 시작했기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 야고보에게서 몇몇 사람이 오기 전에는 그가 이방 사람들과 함께 먹곤 했습니다. 그런데 그들이 오자, 그는 할례를 주장하는 사람들을 두려워해서 물러나 이방 사람들과 따로 떨어져 지내기 시작했습니다.
ko.R: 야고보에게서 몇몇 사람이 오기 전에는 베드로가 유대인이 아닌 신자들과 함께 식사를 하곤 했습니다. 그런데 그들이 오자, 베드로는 슬그머니 물러나서 더 이상 그들과 함께 먹지 않았습니다. 유대인이 아닌 신자들도 할례를 받아야 한다고 주장하는 사람들이 두려웠던 것입니다.

vi.R: Trước khi có mấy người từ chỗ Gia-cơ đến, Phi-e-rơ vẫn thường ăn chung với các tín hữu dân ngoại. Nhưng khi họ đến, ông bắt đầu lánh xa và không còn ăn chung với họ nữa. Ông sợ những người chủ trương rằng các tín hữu dân ngoại phải chịu cắt bì.

pt.L: Pois, antes que chegassem alguns da parte de Tiago, ele comia com os [que eram das] nações; mas, quando chegaram, ele começou a se retirar e a se separar, temendo os da circuncisão.
pt.B: Antes que chegassem algumas pessoas da parte de Tiago, ele costumava comer com os não judeus. Mas, quando elas chegaram, ele começou a se afastar e a se manter à parte, por medo dos que defendiam a circuncisão.
pt.R: Antes que algumas pessoas chegassem da parte de Tiago, Pedro costumava comer com os irmãos não judeus. Mas, depois que elas chegaram, ele começou a se afastar e deixou de comer com eles. Ele tinha medo das pessoas que exigiam que os irmãos não judeus fossem circuncidados.

am.L: ከያዕቆብ ዘንድ አንዳንድ [ሰዎች] ከመምጣታቸው በፊት ከአሕዛብ ጋር ይበላ ነበርና፤ በመጡ ጊዜ ግን ያፈገፍግና ራሱን ይለይ ጀመር፤ ከመገረዝ ወገን የሆኑትን ፈርቶ [ነበር]።

am.R: አንዳንድ ሰዎች ከያዕቆብ ዘንድ ከመምጣታቸው በፊት ጴጥሮስ አይሁድ ካልሆኑ አማኞች ጋር ይበላ ነበር። እነርሱ ከመጡ በኋላ ግን ራሱን እያራቀ ሄደ፤ ከእነርሱም ጋር መብላቱን ተወ። አይሁድ ያልሆኑ አማኞች መገረዝ አለባቸው የሚሉትን ሰዎች ፈራ።

hi.L: क्योंकि याकूब के पास से कुछ [लोगों] के आने से पहले वह अन्यजातियों के साथ खाया करता था; पर जब वे आए, तो वह ख़तनावालों से डरकर पीछे हटने और अपने आप को अलग करने लगा।
hi.B: याकूब के पास से कुछ लोगों के आने से पहले वह अन्यजातियों के साथ खाना खाया करता था। पर जब वे आ गए, तो वह उन लोगों से डरकर, जो ख़तने पर ज़ोर देते थे, पीछे हटने और अपने आप को अलग रखने लगा।

ru.L: Ведь прежде чем пришли некоторые от Иакова, он ел вместе с язычниками; а когда они пришли, стал уклоняться и отделяться, боясь тех, [кто] из обрезания.
ru.B: Пока не пришли некоторые люди от Иакова, он обычно ел вместе с язычниками. Но когда те пришли, он стал отстраняться и держаться отдельно, боясь тех, кто требовал обрезания.
ru.R: Пока от Иакова не пришли некоторые люди, Пётр ел вместе с верующими из других народов. Но когда они пришли, он стал сторониться их и больше с ними не ел. Он боялся людей, которые требовали, чтобы верующие из других народов делали обрезание.

ja.L: というのは、ある人々がヤコブのもとから来る前には、彼は異邦人たちと一緒に食事をしていました。しかし、彼らが来ると、割礼の者たちを恐れて、身を引き、自分を[彼らから]分け始めたのです。
ja.B: ヤコブのところからある人々が来るまでは、彼は異邦人と一緒に食事をしていました。ところが、その人たちが来ると、割礼を求める人々を恐れて、しだいに身を引き、離れて行ったのです。
ja.R: ヤコブのところから何人かの人が来る前は、ペトロはユダヤ人でない信者たちといっしょに食事をしていました。ところが、その人たちが来ると、ペトロは少しずつ離れていき、もうその信者たちと食事をしなくなりました。ユダヤ人でない信者も割礼を受けなければならない、と言い張る人たちを恐れたのです。

uk.L: Бо до того, як прийшли деякі [люди] від Якова, він їв разом із язичниками; а коли вони прийшли, він почав відступати й відокремлюватися, боячись тих, що з обрізання.
uk.B: Поки не прийшли деякі люди від Якова, він їв разом із язичниками. Але коли вони прийшли, він почав відступати й триматися окремо, боячись тих, хто наполягав на обрізанні.
uk.R: Поки не прийшли деякі люди від Якова, Петро їв разом із віруючими неюдеями. Але коли ті прийшли, він почав віддалятися і більше не їв із ними. Він боявся людей, які наполягали, щоб віруючі неюдеї обрізалися.

decisions.choice: eating with Gentiles: sharing meals, probably including the Lord's Supper, across the line the food laws drew
decisions.reason: Many Jews avoided eating with Gentiles, because of the food laws and fear of impurity (Acts 10:28; 11:2-3). συνήσθιεν means to eat together, and in a church of Jews and Gentiles the common meal likely included the Lord's Supper (1 Corinthians 11:20-26). Peter had learned in the house of Cornelius that God accepts Gentiles (Acts 10:34-35).

decisions.choice: he used to eat with them; then he began, step by step, to draw back
alternatives: he ate once; he withdrew at once
decisions.reason: All three verbs are imperfect, the tense for something ongoing: eating with Gentiles was Peter's habit, and his withdrawal was gradual. ὑπέστελλεν can describe pulling back, as a retreating army does.

decisions.choice: people from James: from the Jerusalem church James led, perhaps sent by him
alternatives: sent by James with his authority
decisions.reason: ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου ("from James") could mean sent by James or only that they came from his circle in Jerusalem. Paul does not say that James approved of what followed.

decisions.choice: those who insisted that Gentile believers be circumcised
alternatives: Jews in general, whose pressure on the Jerusalem believers Peter feared
decisions.reason: τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς ("those of the circumcision") can mean Jews in general or a group within the church. Acts uses the same phrase of believers who objected to Peter eating with Gentiles (Acts 11:2), and the issue in Galatians is believers demanding circumcision (2:4; 5:2; 6:12). It could also mean unbelieving Jews whose hostility toward the Jerusalem church Peter feared.

decisions.choice: some [people] (L); some people (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the general "some"; the masculine form does not settle whether women were among them.

decisions.choice: Peter; Gentile believers; no longer ate with them
decisions.reason: Readable names Peter, says that these Gentiles were believers, and says what his separating himself meant in practice (m1).

decisions.choice: algunos
decisions.reason: Spanish "algunos" is, like the Greek word, the general "some", and can stand without a noun, so Literal needs no bracketed word where the English supplies "[people]".

decisions.choice: il mangeait (imparfait); il a commencé à se retirer
decisions.reason: The Greek imperfects describe Peter's habit of eating with Gentiles and a withdrawal that came step by step (m2). French says the habit with the imparfait and the start of the change with "commencer à".

decisions.choice: "những người thuộc phe cắt bì" (L); "những người chủ trương phải cắt bì" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The phrase means those who insisted that Gentile believers be circumcised (m4), not every circumcised Jew, so Vietnamese names the group by what it held. "Chịu cắt bì" alone would include Peter himself.

decisions.choice: com os [que eram das] nações
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "nações" for the word Balanced renders "os não judeus" (as set in 1:16); "comer com as nações" is not Portuguese, so the bracket supplies the people meant.

decisions.choice: os irmãos não judeus
decisions.reason: The English Readable says "Gentile believers". "Irmãos" says they were fellow believers without "crentes", which in Brazil means Protestants.

decisions.choice: стал уклоняться и отделяться
decisions.reason: The imperfects describe a gradual withdrawal (m2); Russian "стал" with the imperfective says that it began and went on.

decisions.choice: "割礼の者たち" (L); "割礼を求める人々" (B); "ユダヤ人でない信者も割礼を受けなければならない、と言い張る人たち" (R)
decisions.reason: Here the phrase is read as those who insisted on circumcising Gentile believers (m4), not simply Jews, so Balanced and Readable say so, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρναβᾶς συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.

records.literal_gloss: And acted hypocritically with him also the rest Jews, so that even Barnabas was carried away of them by the hypocrisy.

en.L: And the rest of the Jews also joined him in playing the hypocrite, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.
en.B: The other Jewish believers joined in his hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was swept along by their pretense.
en.R: The other Jewish believers in Antioch also joined Peter in this pretending. Even Barnabas was carried along by their act.

es.L: Y también los demás judíos actuaron hipócritamente junto con él, de modo que aun Bernabé fue arrastrado por la hipocresía de ellos.
es.B: Los demás creyentes judíos se unieron a su hipocresía, de modo que incluso Bernabé fue arrastrado por su simulación.
es.R: Los otros creyentes judíos de Antioquía también se unieron a Pedro en este fingimiento. Hasta Bernabé se dejó llevar por lo que ellos fingían.

sw.L: Na Wayahudi wengine nao wakaigiza unafiki pamoja naye, hata Barnaba naye akachukuliwa na unafiki wao.
sw.B: Waumini wengine wa Kiyahudi waliungana naye katika unafiki huo, hata Barnaba akachukuliwa na kujifanya kwao.
sw.R: Waumini wengine wa Kiyahudi huko Antiokia nao waliungana na Petro katika kujifanya huku. Hata Barnaba naye alivutwa na kujifanya kwao.

fr.L: Et les autres Juifs aussi ont agi avec lui de manière hypocrite, si bien que même Barnabas a été entraîné par leur hypocrisie.
fr.B: Les autres croyants juifs se sont associés à son hypocrisie, si bien que même Barnabas s’est laissé entraîner par leur double jeu.
fr.R: Les autres croyants juifs d’Antioche ont fait semblant, eux aussi, comme Pierre. Même Barnabas s’est laissé entraîner dans leur comédie.

ko.L: 그리고 나머지 유대인들도 그와 함께 위선을 행하여, 바나바까지도 그들의 위선에 휩쓸려 갔습니다.
ko.B: 다른 유대인 신자들도 그의 위선에 함께했고, 바나바마저 그들의 가식에 휩쓸리고 말았습니다.
ko.R: 안디옥에 있던 다른 유대인 신자들도 베드로와 함께 이렇게 겉으로 꾸미는 행동을 했습니다. 바나바까지도 그들의 거짓 행동에 휩쓸렸습니다.

vi.L: Và những người Do Thái còn lại cũng giả hình với ông, đến nỗi ngay cả Ba-na-ba cũng bị lôi cuốn theo sự giả hình của họ.
vi.B: Các tín hữu Do Thái khác cũng hùa theo ông mà giả hình, đến nỗi ngay cả Ba-na-ba cũng bị lôi cuốn theo sự giả dối của họ.
vi.R: Các tín hữu Do Thái khác ở An-ti-ốt cũng theo Phi-e-rơ mà làm bộ như vậy. Ngay cả Ba-na-ba cũng bị lôi cuốn theo việc làm bộ của họ.

pt.L: E também os demais judeus agiram com hipocrisia junto com ele, de modo que até Barnabé foi arrastado pela hipocrisia deles.
pt.B: Os outros irmãos judeus se juntaram a ele nessa hipocrisia, de modo que até Barnabé foi levado pelo fingimento deles.
pt.R: Os outros irmãos judeus de Antioquia também se juntaram a Pedro nesse fingimento. Até Barnabé se deixou levar pela encenação deles.

am.L: የቀሩትም አይሁድ ደግሞ ከእርሱ ጋር አብረው ግብዝነት አደረጉ፤ ስለዚህ በርናባስ እንኳ በግብዝነታቸው ተወሰደ።
am.B: ሌሎቹም አይሁድ አማኞች በግብዝነቱ ተባበሩት፤ ስለዚህ በርናባስ እንኳ በማስመሰላቸው ተሳበ።
am.R: በአንጾኪያ ያሉት ሌሎቹ አይሁድ አማኞችም በዚህ ማስመሰል ከጴጥሮስ ጋር ተባበሩ። በርናባስ እንኳ በድርጊታቸው ተሳበ።

hi.L: और बाक़ी यहूदियों ने भी उसके साथ पाखंड किया, यहाँ तक कि बरनबास भी उनके पाखंड में बह गया।
hi.B: दूसरे यहूदी विश्वासी भी उसके इस पाखंड में शामिल हो गए, यहाँ तक कि बरनबास भी उनके दिखावे में बह गया।
hi.R: अन्ताकिया के दूसरे यहूदी विश्वासी भी इस दिखावे में पतरस के साथ हो गए। बरनबास भी उनके इस नाटक में बह गया।

ru.L: И вместе с ним лицемерили и прочие иудеи, так что даже Варнава был увлечён их лицемерием.
ru.B: Другие верующие иудеи тоже присоединились к его лицемерию, так что даже Варнава поддался их притворству.
ru.R: Другие верующие иудеи в Антиохии тоже стали притворяться вместе с Петром. Даже Варнаву увлекло их притворство.

ja.L: そして、ほかのユダヤ人たちも彼と一緒に偽善を行い、バルナバまでもが、彼らの偽善に引きずり込まれてしまいました。
ja.B: ほかのユダヤ人の信者たちも彼の偽善に加わり、バルナバまでもが、彼らの見せかけに流されてしまいました。
ja.R: アンティオキアにいたほかのユダヤ人の信者たちも、ペトロといっしょに、うわべだけのふるまいをしました。バルナバまでが、その人たちのふるまいに引きずられてしまいました。

uk.L: І разом із ним лицемірили й інші юдеї, так що навіть Варнава був захоплений їхнім лицемірством.
uk.B: Інші віруючі юдеї приєдналися до його лицемірства, так що навіть Варнаву захопило їхнє удавання.
uk.R: Інші віруючі юдеї в Антіохії теж приєдналися до Петра в цьому удаванні. Навіть Варнаву захопила їхня гра.

decisions.choice: hypocrisy: acting a part, behaving against what they believed
decisions.reason: ὑπόκρισις comes from the stage: playing a role. Peter and the others still believed that God accepted Gentile believers, yet acted as if they were unclean. Paul's charge is that their conduct contradicted their convictions, not that their faith was false.

decisions.choice: the rest of the Jews: the other Jewish believers in the Antioch church
decisions.reason: The people joining Peter in withdrawing from the shared meals are members of the church who had been eating with Gentile believers.

decisions.choice: even Barnabas: Paul's partner in the mission to the Gentiles
decisions.reason: Barnabas had gone with Paul to Jerusalem and shared in the agreement to go to the Gentiles (verses 1 and 9). καὶ ("even") marks how serious it was that he too was carried along.

decisions.choice: Jewish believers (B); Jewish believers in Antioch (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who these Jews were (m2).

decisions.choice: pretense (B); pretending, act (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "hypocrisy" once and "pretense" for the second occurrence to avoid repeating it; Readable uses plain words for acting a part (m1).

decisions.choice: "giả hình" (L, B); "làm bộ" (R)
decisions.reason: "Giả hình" is to act a part against what one believes (m1), the word the Vietnamese Gospels use for hypocrites; Readable says "làm bộ", to put on an act.

decisions.choice: ግብዝነት (L, B); ማስመሰል (pretense, B, R)
decisions.reason: "ግብዝነት", the word used for the Gospels' hypocrites, is kept at Literal and in Balanced's first clause; Balanced and Readable then say "ማስመሰል", acting a part against what one believes (meaning decision m1), as the English says "pretense".
"पाखंड" is the word the Gospels use for hypocrites; Balanced varies the second occurrence, and Readable uses plain words for acting a part (meaning decision m1), as the English does.

decisions.choice: "偽善" (L, B; "見せかけ" for the second at B); "うわべだけのふるまい" (R)
decisions.reason: Acting a part against what they believed (m1). "偽善" is the guide's word; Readable says what it was in everyday words.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων· Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς καὶ οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς, πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις Ἰουδαΐζειν;

records.literal_gloss: But when I saw that not they are walking straight toward the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas before all: If you a Jew being like a Gentile and not like a Jew live, how the Gentiles do you compel to Judaize?

en.L: But when I saw that they were not walking straight according to the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of [them] all, "If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how [is it that] you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
en.B: But when I saw that they were not walking in step with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, "You are a Jew, yet you live like a Gentile and not like a Jew. How then can you force the Gentiles to live like Jews?"
en.R: I saw that they were not living in line with the truth of the good news. So I spoke to Peter in front of everyone. I said, "You are a Jew, but you have been living like a Gentile, not like a Jew. So how can you force Gentiles to live like Jews?"

es.L: Pero cuando vi que no andaban rectamente conforme a la verdad del evangelio, dije a Cefas delante de todos: «Si tú, siendo judío, vives como gentil y no como judío, ¿cómo obligas a los gentiles a vivir como judíos?».
es.B: Pero cuando vi que no caminaban en línea con la verdad del evangelio, dije a Cefas delante de todos: «Tú eres judío, y sin embargo vives como gentil y no como judío. ¿Cómo puedes, entonces, obligar a los gentiles a vivir como judíos?».
es.R: Vi que no estaban viviendo de acuerdo con la verdad de la buena noticia. Así que hablé con Pedro delante de todos. Le dije: «Tú eres judío, pero has estado viviendo como gentil, no como judío. Entonces, ¿cómo puedes obligar a los gentiles a vivir como judíos?».

sw.L: Lakini nilipoona kwamba hawaendi sawasawa kulingana na kweli ya Injili, nilimwambia Kefa mbele ya wote, "Ikiwa wewe, uliye Myahudi, unaishi kama mtu wa mataifa na si kama Myahudi, unawalazimishaje watu wa mataifa kuishi kama Wayahudi?"
sw.B: Lakini nilipoona kwamba mwenendo wao haupatani na kweli ya Injili, nilimwambia Kefa mbele yao wote, "Wewe ni Myahudi, lakini unaishi kama mtu wa mataifa na si kama Myahudi. Basi unawezaje kuwalazimisha watu wa mataifa kuishi kama Wayahudi?"
sw.R: Niliona kwamba hawakuwa wakiishi kulingana na kweli ya Habari Njema. Kwa hiyo nilizungumza na Petro mbele ya kila mtu. Nilimwambia, "Wewe ni Myahudi, lakini umekuwa ukiishi kama mtu wa mataifa, si kama Myahudi. Basi unawezaje kuwalazimisha watu wa mataifa kuishi kama Wayahudi?"

fr.L: Mais quand j’ai vu qu’ils ne marchaient pas droit selon la vérité de l’Évangile, j’ai dit à Céphas devant tous : « Si toi, qui es juif, tu vis à la manière des nations et non à la manière des Juifs, comment peux-tu contraindre les nations à vivre comme les Juifs ? »
fr.B: Mais quand j’ai vu qu’ils ne marchaient pas droit, en accord avec la vérité de l’Évangile, j’ai dit à Céphas devant tout le monde : « Tu es juif, et pourtant tu vis comme un non-Juif et non comme un Juif. Comment peux-tu donc forcer les non-Juifs à vivre comme des Juifs ? »
fr.R: J’ai vu que leur conduite ne s’accordait pas avec la vérité de la bonne nouvelle. Alors j’ai parlé à Pierre devant tout le monde. Je lui ai dit : « Tu es juif, mais tu as vécu comme un non-Juif, et pas comme un Juif. Alors comment peux-tu obliger les non-Juifs à vivre comme des Juifs ? »

ko.L: 그러나 나는 그들이 복음의 진리를 따라 바르게 걷지 않는 것을 보고, 모든 [사람] 앞에서 게바에게 말했습니다. "당신은 유대인이면서도 유대인처럼 살지 않고 이방 사람처럼 살면서, 어떻게 이방 사람들에게 유대인처럼 살라고 강요합니까?"
ko.B: 그러나 나는 그들이 복음의 진리에 맞게 바르게 행하지 않는 것을 보고, 모든 사람 앞에서 게바에게 말했습니다. "당신은 유대인인데도 유대인처럼 살지 않고 이방 사람처럼 살고 있습니다. 그런데 어떻게 이방 사람들에게 유대인처럼 살라고 강요할 수 있습니까?"
ko.R: 나는 그들이 기쁜 소식의 진리에 맞게 살지 않는 것을 보았습니다. 그래서 모든 사람 앞에서 베드로에게 말했습니다. "당신은 유대인이지만, 지금까지 유대인처럼 살지 않고 유대인이 아닌 사람처럼 살아 왔습니다. 그런데 어떻게 유대인이 아닌 사람들에게 유대인처럼 살라고 강요할 수 있습니까?"

vi.L: Nhưng khi tôi thấy họ không bước đi ngay thẳng theo chân lý của Tin Lành, tôi nói với Sê-pha trước mặt mọi người: "Nếu anh là người Do Thái mà sống như dân ngoại, không như người Do Thái, thì sao anh lại ép các dân ngoại phải sống như người Do Thái?"
vi.B: Nhưng khi thấy họ không bước đi đúng theo chân lý của Tin Lành, tôi nói với Sê-pha trước mặt mọi người: "Anh là người Do Thái, thế mà anh sống như dân ngoại chứ không như người Do Thái. Vậy làm sao anh có thể ép các dân ngoại sống như người Do Thái?"
vi.R: Tôi thấy họ không sống theo đúng chân lý của Tin Lành. Vì vậy tôi nói với Phi-e-rơ trước mặt mọi người: "Anh là người Do Thái, nhưng anh vẫn sống như dân ngoại, không như người Do Thái. Vậy làm sao anh có thể ép dân ngoại phải sống như người Do Thái?"

pt.L: Mas, quando vi que eles não andavam direito segundo a verdade do evangelho, eu disse a Cefas diante de todos: "Se você, sendo judeu, vive à maneira das nações e não à maneira judaica, como [é que] obriga as nações a viver como judeus?"
pt.B: Mas, quando vi que eles não estavam andando de acordo com a verdade do evangelho, eu disse a Cefas na frente de todos: "Você é judeu, mas vive como um não judeu, e não como judeu. Então como pode obrigar os não judeus a viver como judeus?"
pt.R: Eu vi que eles não estavam vivendo de acordo com a verdade das boas-novas. Por isso falei com Pedro na frente de todos. Eu disse: "Você é judeu, mas tem vivido como um não judeu, e não como judeu. Então como você pode obrigar os não judeus a viver como judeus?"

am.L: ነገር ግን በወንጌል እውነት መሠረት ቀጥ ብለው እንደማይሄዱ ባየሁ ጊዜ፣ በሁሉ ፊት ኬፋን እንዲህ አልኩት፦ «አንተ አይሁዳዊ ሆነህ ሳለ እንደ አሕዛብ እንጂ እንደ አይሁድ ካልኖርክ፣ አሕዛብን እንደ አይሁድ እንዲኖሩ እንዴት ታስገድዳቸዋለህ?»
am.B: ነገር ግን ከወንጌል እውነት ጋር ተስማምተው እንደማይሄዱ ባየሁ ጊዜ፣ በሁሉም ፊት ኬፋን እንዲህ አልኩት፦ «አንተ አይሁዳዊ ነህ፤ ሆኖም እንደ አይሁድ ሳይሆን እንደ አሕዛብ ትኖራለህ። ታዲያ አሕዛብ እንደ አይሁድ እንዲኖሩ እንዴት ታስገድዳቸዋለህ?»
am.R: ከምሥራቹ እውነት ጋር ተስማምተው እንደማይኖሩ አየሁ። ስለዚህ በሁሉም ሰው ፊት ጴጥሮስን አነጋገርኩት። እንዲህም አልኩት፦ «አንተ አይሁዳዊ ነህ፤ ነገር ግን እንደ አይሁዳዊ ሳይሆን አይሁዳዊ እንዳልሆነ ሰው ስትኖር ቆይተሃል። ታዲያ አይሁድ ያልሆኑትን እንደ አይሁድ እንዲኖሩ እንዴት ታስገድዳቸዋለህ?»

hi.L: पर जब मैंने देखा कि वे सुसमाचार के सत्य के अनुसार सीधी चाल नहीं चल रहे, तो मैंने सब के सामने केफ़ा से कहा, "यदि तुम यहूदी होकर अन्यजातियों की तरह जीते हो, न कि यहूदियों की तरह, तो तुम अन्यजातियों को यहूदियों की तरह जीने के लिए कैसे विवश करते हो?"
hi.B: पर जब मैंने देखा कि वे सुसमाचार के सत्य के अनुसार ठीक से नहीं चल रहे, तो मैंने सब के सामने केफ़ा से कहा, "तुम यहूदी हो, फिर भी अन्यजातियों की तरह जीते हो, यहूदियों की तरह नहीं। तो तुम अन्यजातियों को यहूदियों की तरह जीने के लिए कैसे मजबूर कर सकते हो?"
hi.R: मैंने देखा कि वे सुसमाचार के सच के अनुसार नहीं जी रहे थे। इसलिए मैंने सब के सामने पतरस से बात की। मैंने कहा, "तुम यहूदी हो, पर तुम ग़ैर-यहूदियों की तरह जीते आए हो, यहूदियों की तरह नहीं। तो तुम ग़ैर-यहूदियों को यहूदियों की तरह जीने के लिए कैसे मजबूर कर सकते हो?"

ru.L: Но когда я увидел, что они не прямо ходят по истине Евангелия, я сказал Кифе перед всеми: «Если ты, будучи иудеем, живёшь по-язычески, а не по-иудейски, как [же] ты принуждаешь язычников жить по-иудейски?»
ru.B: Но когда я увидел, что они не идут прямым путём, согласным с истиной Евангелия, я сказал Кифе при всех: «Ты иудей, но живёшь как язычник, а не как иудей. Как же ты можешь заставлять язычников жить как иудеи?»
ru.R: Я увидел, что они живут не так, как учит правда Радостной вести. Поэтому я заговорил с Петром при всех. Я сказал: «Ты иудей, но ты жил как человек из другого народа, а не как иудей. Как же ты можешь заставлять людей из других народов жить как иудеи?»

ja.L: しかし、彼らが福音の真理に沿ってまっすぐに歩んでいないのを見たとき、わたしは皆の前でケファに言いました。「あなたはユダヤ人でありながら、ユダヤ人のようにではなく異邦人のように生きているのに、どうして異邦人にユダヤ人のように生きることを強いるのか？」
ja.B: しかし、彼らが福音の真理にかなった歩みをしていないのを見て、わたしは皆の前でケファに言いました。「あなたはユダヤ人なのに、ユダヤ人のようにではなく、異邦人のように生活している。それなのに、どうして異邦人にユダヤ人のように生活するよう強いるのか？」
ja.R: わたしは、その人たちが本当の良い知らせにふさわしい生き方をしていないのを見ました。そこで、みんなの前でペトロに言いました。「あなたはユダヤ人なのに、これまでユダヤ人のようにではなく、ユダヤ人でない人のように暮らしてきた。それなのに、どうしてユダヤ人でない人たちに、ユダヤ人のように暮らせと無理に求めるのか？」

uk.L: Але коли я побачив, що вони не ходять прямо за істиною Євангелія, я сказав Кифі перед усіма: «Якщо ти, будучи юдеєм, живеш як язичник, а не як юдей, то як [це] ти змушуєш язичників жити як юдеї?»
uk.B: Але коли я побачив, що вони не йдуть у ногу з істиною Євангелія, я сказав Кифі перед усіма: «Ти юдей, а живеш як язичник, а не як юдей. Як же ти можеш змушувати язичників жити як юдеї?»
uk.R: Я побачив, що вони живуть не так, як вимагає правда Доброї звістки. Тож я заговорив до Петра перед усіма. Я сказав: «Ти юдей, але жив як неюдей, а не як юдей. То як ти можеш змушувати неюдеїв жити як юдеї?»

decisions.choice: Paul's words to Cephas are given as ending with this verse
alternatives: his words to Cephas run on to the end of the chapter (verse 21)
they run to the end of verse 15 or 16
decisions.reason: Greek has no quotation marks, so where Paul's words at Antioch end is not marked. Verses 15-16 still speak of "we" who are Jews, which fits the conversation with Cephas, but by verse 21 Paul is plainly addressing the Galatians' situation. The quotation is closed at the end of verse 14, where the direct question to Cephas ends; verses 15-21 may still continue what Paul said to him, and the meaning of those verses is the same either way.

decisions.choice: not walking straight: their conduct did not match the truth of the gospel
alternatives: not making progress toward the truth
decisions.reason: ὀρθοποδέω means to walk straight or upright. With πρὸς it means conduct in line with the gospel's truth: by separating from Gentile believers they were acting as if the gospel did not make Jews and Gentiles one (3:28).

decisions.choice: you live like a Gentile: Peter's settled way of life, free of the food laws, until his recent withdrawal
alternatives: you lived like a Gentile in the past
decisions.reason: ζῇς is present tense. Peter had made a habit of eating with Gentiles (verse 12) and was in principle still free of the food laws; his withdrawal did not change what he believed. The inconsistency is Paul's point.

decisions.choice: compel the Gentiles to live like Jews: put pressure on them, by his example, to keep the Jewish law
alternatives: to become Jewish converts by formal ceremony
decisions.reason: ἰουδαΐζω means to adopt Jewish customs, such as the food laws and circumcision. Peter gave no order, but when the leading apostle would not eat with them, Gentile believers were left with one way back to the table: to live as Jews. ἀναγκάζεις is the verb used of Titus in verse 3.

decisions.choice: Cephas (L, B); Peter (R)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9.

decisions.choice: "You are a Jew, yet you live like a Gentile ... How then can you ...?"
alternatives: If you, being a Jew, live like a Gentile ..., how ...?
decisions.reason: The "if" states something both men knew to be true, so Balanced and Readable state it as a fact and then ask the question.

decisions.choice: tú, no plural_you setting
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to Cephas alone, with singular verbs, so Spanish uses "tú" and these words take no ustedes/vosotros setting.

decisions.choice: comme un non-Juif; les non-Juifs (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here Paul speaks of one man's way of life and of the Gentile believers at Antioch, not of the nations as peoples, so Balanced says "non-Juif", as set out in 1:16. Literal keeps "nations" for the same Greek root.

decisions.choice: Paul speaks to Cephas as "당신" in 합쇼체
decisions.reason: Paul rebukes a fellow apostle in public, as an equal. Korean 합쇼체 with "당신" is formal and direct without being insulting, which fits a public rebuke between equals; 해라체 would make Paul talk down to Peter, which the scene does not suggest. A reviewer may prefer another way of addressing him.

decisions.choice: "anh" for Cephas in Paul's words
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to a fellow apostle and equal, face to face, so Vietnamese uses "anh", the plain respectful word between colleagues; "ông", used for Peter in the narrative, would be too distant in direct speech.

decisions.choice: "bước đi ngay thẳng" (L); "bước đi đúng theo" (B)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep Paul's picture of walking straight, a way of life that matches the truth (m2); Readable says "sống".

decisions.choice: você
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to Peter as one apostle to another, so Portuguese uses "você" at every level (style section 4); "tu" is kept for words addressed to God or Christ, and "o senhor" would make Peter Paul's superior.

decisions.choice: አንተ (you, familiar) from Paul to Cephas
decisions.reason: Paul speaks to a fellow apostle as an equal, and rebukes him in public; the familiar "አንተ", which Amharic uses between equals, fits both.

decisions.choice: Paul says "तुम" to Cephas
decisions.reason: Two apostles speaking as equals; believers say "तुम" among themselves (style guide, section 7b, Acts).

decisions.choice: "सीधी चाल नहीं चल रहे"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of walking straight; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Paul's words to Cephas in the plain style ("強いるのか"), inside the polite letter
decisions.reason: Paul rebukes a fellow apostle to his face before the whole church; the plain style is how one says that among equals in Japanese, and it sets the reported speech off from the letter's です・ます体.

decisions.choice: "まっすぐに歩んでいない" (L); "かなった歩みをしていない" (B); "ふさわしい生き方をしていない" (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek pictures walking straight (m2). Literal keeps the picture, Balanced keeps "歩み", the church word for a way of life, and Readable says it plainly.

source.text: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί, εἰδότες δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται πᾶσα σάρξ.

records.literal_gloss: We by nature Jews and not of Gentiles sinners, \v 16 knowing but that not is justified a man by works of law if not through faith of Jesus Christ, also we in Christ Jesus believed, so that we might be justified by faith of Christ and not by works of law, because by works of law not will be justified all flesh.

en.L: We [are] Jews by birth and not sinners from [the] Gentiles, \v 16 but knowing that a person is not justified by works of [the] law except through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, we also have believed in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} Jesus, so that we might be justified by faith in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and not by works of [the] law, because by works of [the] law no flesh will be justified.
en.B: We ourselves are Jews by birth, not Gentile sinners. \v 16 Yet we know that no one is justified by works of the law; a person is justified only through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. So we too have believed in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus, in order to be justified by faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} and not by works of the law, because no human being will be justified by works of the law.
en.R: We ourselves were born Jews. We are not Gentiles, the people Jews call sinners. \v 16 But we know that no one is put right with God by doing what the law commands. People are put right with God only through faith in Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. So we too have believed in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} Jesus. We did this so that we would be put right with God by faith in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, and not by doing what the law commands. For no one will be put right with God by doing what the law commands.

es.L: Nosotros [somos] judíos de nacimiento y no pecadores de entre [los] gentiles, \v 16 pero, sabiendo que una persona no es justificada por obras de [la] ley sino por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}, también nosotros hemos creído en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, para ser justificados por la fe en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} y no por obras de [la] ley, porque por obras de [la] ley ninguna carne será justificada.
es.B: Nosotros mismos somos judíos de nacimiento, no pecadores gentiles. \v 16 Pero sabemos que nadie es justificado por las obras de la ley; una persona es justificada solamente por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por eso también nosotros hemos creído en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}, para ser justificados por la fe en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} y no por las obras de la ley, porque ningún ser humano será justificado por las obras de la ley.
es.R: Nosotros mismos nacimos judíos. No somos gentiles, la gente a la que los judíos llaman pecadores. \v 16 Pero sabemos que Dios no declara justo a nadie por hacer lo que manda la ley. Dios declara justas a las personas solo por medio de la fe en {{christos:Jesucristo|Jesús, el Mesías}}. Por eso también nosotros hemos creído en {{christos:Cristo Jesús|el Mesías Jesús}}. Lo hicimos para que Dios nos declarara justos por la fe en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, y no por hacer lo que manda la ley. Porque Dios no declarará justo a nadie por hacer lo que manda la ley.

sw.L: Sisi [ni] Wayahudi kwa kuzaliwa na si wenye dhambi kutoka [kwa] watu wa mataifa, \v 16 lakini tukijua kwamba mtu hahesabiwi haki kwa matendo ya sheria ila kwa njia ya imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sisi nasi tumemwamini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ili tuhesabiwe haki kwa imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} na si kwa matendo ya sheria, kwa sababu kwa matendo ya sheria hakuna mwili utakaohesabiwa haki.
sw.B: Sisi wenyewe ni Wayahudi kwa kuzaliwa, si wenye dhambi wa mataifa. \v 16 Hata hivyo tunajua kwamba hakuna mtu anayehesabiwa haki kwa matendo ya sheria; mtu huhesabiwa haki kwa njia ya imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} tu. Kwa hiyo sisi pia tumemwamini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu, ili tuhesabiwe haki kwa imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} wala si kwa matendo ya sheria, kwa sababu hakuna binadamu atakayehesabiwa haki kwa matendo ya sheria.
sw.R: Sisi wenyewe tulizaliwa Wayahudi. Sisi si watu wa mataifa, wale ambao Wayahudi huwaita wenye dhambi. \v 16 Lakini tunajua kwamba hakuna mtu anayehesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru. Watu huhesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa imani katika Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} tu. Kwa hiyo sisi nasi tumemwamini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} Yesu. Tulifanya hivyo ili tuhesabiwe haki na Mungu kwa imani katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, wala si kwa kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru. Kwa maana hakuna mtu atakayehesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru.

fr.L: Nous, nous [sommes] juifs de naissance et non pécheurs d’entre les nations, \v 16 mais sachant qu’un {{gender:être humain|homme}} n’est pas justifié par les œuvres de la Loi, si ce n’est par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, nous aussi nous avons cru {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, afin d’être justifiés par la foi {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} et non par les œuvres de la Loi, parce que par les œuvres de la Loi nulle chair ne sera justifiée.
fr.B: Nous-mêmes, nous sommes juifs de naissance, et non des pécheurs issus des nations. \v 16 Pourtant, nous savons que personne n’est justifié par les œuvres de la Loi : on n’est justifié que par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. C’est pourquoi nous aussi, nous avons cru {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus, afin d’être justifiés par la foi {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} et non par les œuvres de la Loi, puisque aucun être humain ne sera justifié par les œuvres de la Loi.
fr.R: Nous-mêmes, nous sommes nés juifs. Nous ne sommes pas des non-Juifs, ces gens que les Juifs appellent des pécheurs. \v 16 Mais nous savons que personne n’est déclaré juste par Dieu parce qu’il fait ce que la Loi ordonne. Dieu déclare les gens justes seulement par la foi en Jésus {{christos:Christ|le Messie}}. C’est pourquoi nous aussi, nous avons cru {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}} Jésus. Nous l’avons fait pour être déclarés justes par Dieu grâce à la foi {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, et non parce que nous faisons ce que la Loi ordonne. Car personne ne sera déclaré juste par Dieu parce qu’il fait ce que la Loi ordonne.

ko.L: 우리는 본래 유대인이요 이방 [출신] 죄인들이 아닙니다. \v 16 그러나 사람이 율법의 행위들로는 의롭다고 인정받지 못하고, 오직 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음을 통해서 [인정받는다는 것을] 알기에, 우리도 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수를 믿었습니다. 이는 우리가 율법의 행위들로가 아니라 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정받으려는 것입니다. 율법의 행위들로는 어떤 육체도 의롭다고 인정받지 못할 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.B: 우리는 나면서부터 유대인이고, 이방 죄인들이 아닙니다. \v 16 그러나 우리는 사람이 율법의 행위로 의롭다고 인정받는 것이 아니라는 것을 압니다. 사람은 오직 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정받습니다. 그래서 우리도 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수를 믿었습니다. 율법의 행위가 아니라 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음으로 의롭다고 인정받으려는 것입니다. 율법의 행위로는 아무도 의롭다고 인정받지 못할 것이기 때문입니다.
ko.R: 우리는 유대인으로 태어났습니다. 우리는 유대인들이 죄인이라고 부르는, 유대인이 아닌 사람들이 아닙니다. \v 16 그러나 우리는 율법이 명령하는 것을 행해서 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받을 수 있는 사람은 아무도 없다는 것을 압니다. 사람은 오직 예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음으로만 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받습니다. 그래서 우리도 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 예수를 믿었습니다. 율법이 명령하는 것을 행해서가 아니라, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음으로 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받으려고 그렇게 했습니다. 율법이 명령하는 것을 행해서 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받을 사람은 아무도 없기 때문입니다.

vi.L: Chúng ta là người Do Thái từ khi sinh ra, chứ không phải tội nhân từ các dân ngoại, \v 16 nhưng biết rằng con người không được xưng công chính bởi những việc làm của luật pháp, mà chỉ qua đức tin nơi Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, chính chúng ta cũng đã tin vào {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} Giê-xu, để được xưng công chính bởi đức tin nơi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, chứ không bởi những việc làm của luật pháp, vì bởi những việc làm của luật pháp sẽ không có xác thịt nào được xưng công chính.
vi.B: Chính chúng ta là người Do Thái từ khi sinh ra, không phải là dân ngoại tội lỗi. \v 16 Nhưng chúng ta biết rằng không ai được xưng công chính nhờ làm những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi; con người chỉ được xưng công chính qua đức tin nơi Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Vì vậy, chính chúng ta cũng đã tin vào Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}, để được xưng công chính bởi đức tin nơi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, chứ không nhờ làm những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi, vì không một người nào sẽ được xưng công chính nhờ làm những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi.
vi.R: Chính chúng ta sinh ra là người Do Thái. Chúng ta không phải là dân ngoại, những người mà người Do Thái gọi là tội nhân. \v 16 Nhưng chúng ta biết rằng không ai được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính nhờ làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy. Người ta chỉ được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính qua đức tin nơi Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Vì vậy chính chúng ta cũng đã tin vào Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}. Chúng ta làm vậy để được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính bởi đức tin nơi {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, chứ không phải nhờ làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy. Vì không ai sẽ được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính nhờ làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy.

pt.L: Nós [somos] judeus de nascimento e não pecadores dentre as nações, \v 16 mas, sabendo que uma pessoa não é justificada por obras da Lei, a não ser por meio da fé em Jesus {{christos:Cristo|Messias}}, também nós cremos {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus, para que fôssemos justificados pela fé {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}}, e não por obras da Lei, porque por obras da Lei nenhuma carne será justificada.
pt.B: Nós mesmos somos judeus de nascimento, e não pecadores como os não judeus. \v 16 Mesmo assim, sabemos que ninguém é declarado justo pelas obras da Lei; uma pessoa é declarada justa somente por meio da fé em Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}. Por isso nós também cremos {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus, para sermos declarados justos pela fé {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}}, e não pelas obras da Lei, porque nenhum ser humano será declarado justo pelas obras da Lei.
pt.R: Nós mesmos nascemos judeus. Não somos de outros povos, que os judeus chamam de pecadores. \v 16 Mas sabemos que ninguém é aceito por Deus como justo por fazer o que a Lei manda. As pessoas são aceitas por Deus como justas somente por meio da fé em Jesus {{christos:Cristo|o Messias}}. Por isso nós também acreditamos {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}} Jesus. Fizemos isso para sermos aceitos por Deus como justos pela fé {{christos:em Cristo|no Messias}}, e não por fazermos o que a Lei manda. Pois ninguém será aceito por Deus como justo por fazer o que a Lei manda.

am.L: እኛ በተፈጥሮ አይሁድ [ነን]፤ ከአሕዛብም ኃጢአተኞች አይደለንም፤ \v 16 ነገር ግን ሰው በኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} [ባለ] እምነት በኩል ካልሆነ በቀር በሕግ ሥራ እንደማይጸድቅ አውቀን፣ እኛ ደግሞ በሕግ ሥራ ሳይሆን {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} [ባለ] እምነት እንድንጸድቅ {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} ኢየሱስ አመንን፤ በሕግ ሥራ ሥጋ ሁሉ አይጸድቅምና።
am.B: እኛ ራሳችን በትውልድ አይሁድ ነን እንጂ ከአሕዛብ የሆንን ኃጢአተኞች አይደለንም። \v 16 ሆኖም ማንም በሕግ ሥራ እንደማይጸድቅ እናውቃለን፤ ሰው የሚጸድቀው በኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በማመን ብቻ ነው። ስለዚህ እኛም በሕግ ሥራ ሳይሆን {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} በማመን እንድንጸድቅ {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} ኢየሱስ አምነናል፤ ምክንያቱም በሕግ ሥራ ማንም ሰው አይጸድቅም።
am.R: እኛ ራሳችን አይሁድ ሆነን ተወለድን። አይሁድ ኃጢአተኞች ብለው ከሚጠሯቸው አይሁድ ካልሆኑ ሕዝቦች አይደለንም። \v 16 ነገር ግን ሕጉ የሚለውን በማድረግ ማንም ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት እንደማያገኝ እናውቃለን። ሰዎች ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት የሚያገኙት በኢየሱስ {{christos:ክርስቶስ|መሲሕ}} በማመን ብቻ ነው። ስለዚህ እኛም {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} ኢየሱስ አምነናል። ይህን ያደረግነው ሕጉ የሚለውን በማድረግ ሳይሆን {{christos:በክርስቶስ|በመሲሕ}} በማመን ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት እንድናገኝ ነው። ሕጉ የሚለውን በማድረግ ማንም ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት አያገኝምና።

hi.L: हम जन्म से यहूदी हैं, और अन्यजातियों में से पापी नहीं, \v 16 पर यह जानकर कि मनुष्य व्यवस्था के कामों से धर्मी नहीं ठहराया जाता, सिवाय यीशु मसीह पर विश्वास के द्वारा, हमने भी मसीह यीशु पर विश्वास किया, ताकि हम मसीह पर विश्वास से धर्मी ठहराए जाएँ, न कि व्यवस्था के कामों से, क्योंकि व्यवस्था के कामों से कोई भी शरीरधारी धर्मी नहीं ठहराया जाएगा।
hi.B: हम तो जन्म से यहूदी हैं, अन्यजाति पापी नहीं। \v 16 फिर भी हम जानते हैं कि कोई भी व्यवस्था के कामों से धर्मी नहीं ठहराया जाता; मनुष्य केवल यीशु मसीह पर विश्वास के द्वारा धर्मी ठहराया जाता है। इसलिए हमने भी मसीह यीशु पर विश्वास किया, ताकि हम व्यवस्था के कामों से नहीं, बल्कि मसीह पर विश्वास से धर्मी ठहराए जाएँ, क्योंकि व्यवस्था के कामों से कोई भी मनुष्य धर्मी नहीं ठहराया जाएगा।
hi.R: हम ख़ुद जन्म से यहूदी हैं। हम ग़ैर-यहूदी नहीं हैं, जिन्हें यहूदी पापी कहते हैं। \v 16 पर हम जानते हैं कि व्यवस्था जो कहती है, वह करके कोई भी परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में सही नहीं ठहरता। लोग केवल यीशु मसीह पर विश्वास के द्वारा परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में सही ठहराए जाते हैं। इसलिए हमने भी मसीह यीशु पर विश्वास किया है। हमने यह इसलिए किया कि हम मसीह पर विश्वास के द्वारा परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में सही ठहराए जाएँ, व्यवस्था की बातें मानकर नहीं। क्योंकि व्यवस्था जो कहती है, वह करके कोई भी परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में सही नहीं ठहराया जाएगा।

ru.L: Мы по природе иудеи, а не грешники из язычников, \v 16 но, зная, что человек оправдывается не делами Закона, а только через веру в Иисуса {{christos:Христа|Мессию}}, и мы уверовали в {{christos:Христа|Мессию}} Иисуса, чтобы нам оправдаться верой в {{christos:Христа|Мессию}}, а не делами Закона, потому что делами Закона не оправдается никакая плоть.
ru.B: Мы сами иудеи по рождению, а не грешники из язычников. \v 16 Но мы знаем, что никто не оправдывается делами Закона: человек оправдывается только через веру в Иисуса {{christos:Христа|Мессию}}. Поэтому и мы поверили в {{christos:Христа|Мессию}} Иисуса, чтобы быть оправданными верой в {{christos:Христа|Мессию}}, а не делами Закона, потому что никто из людей не будет оправдан делами Закона.
ru.R: Мы сами родились иудеями. Мы не из других народов, которых иудеи называют грешниками. \v 16 Но мы знаем, что Бог оправдывает человека перед собой не за то, что тот делает то, что говорит Закон. Бог оправдывает людей только через веру в Иисуса {{christos:Христа|Мессию}}. Поэтому и мы поверили в {{christos:Христа|Мессию}} Иисуса. Мы сделали это, чтобы Бог оправдал нас через веру в {{christos:Христа|Мессию}}, а не за то, что мы делаем то, что говорит Закон. Ведь никто не будет оправдан перед Богом за то, что делает то, что говорит Закон.

ja.L: わたしたちは生まれながらのユダヤ人であって、異邦人出の罪人ではありません。\v 16 しかし、人は律法の行いによっては義とされず、ただイエス・{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}への信仰を通して[義とされる]ことを知っているので、わたしたち自身も{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}・イエスを信じました。それは、律法の行いによってではなく、{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}への信仰によって義とされるためです。律法の行いによっては、どの肉も義とされないのですから。
ja.B: わたしたちは生まれながらのユダヤ人であって、異邦人のような罪人ではありません。\v 16 けれども、わたしたちが知っているとおり、律法の行いによって義とされる人はいません。人はただ、イエス・{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}への信仰によって義とされるのです。だからこそ、わたしたちも{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}・イエスを信じました。律法の行いによってではなく、{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}への信仰によって義とされるためです。律法の行いによって義とされる人間は、一人もいないのです。
ja.R: わたしたちは、生まれたときからユダヤ人です。ユダヤ人が罪人と呼ぶ、ユダヤ人でない人々ではありません。\v 16 けれども、わたしたちは知っています。律法の命じることを行っても、神に正しい者と認められる人はいません。人が神に正しい者と認められるのは、ただイエス・{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}を信じる信仰によるのです。だから、わたしたちも{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}・イエスを信じました。律法の命じることを行うことによってではなく、{{christos:キリスト|メシア}}を信じる信仰によって、神に正しい者と認められるためです。律法の命じることを行って神に正しい者と認められる人は、一人もいないからです。

uk.L: Ми з природи юдеї, а не грішники з язичників, \v 16 але, знаючи, що людина виправдовується не ділами Закону, а тільки через віру в Ісуса {{christos:Христа|Месію}}, і ми увірували в {{christos:Христа|Месію}} Ісуса, щоб бути виправданими вірою в {{christos:Христа|Месію}}, а не ділами Закону, бо ділами Закону не виправдається жодне тіло.
uk.B: Ми самі юдеї з народження, а не грішники з язичників. \v 16 Проте ми знаємо, що жодна людина не виправдовується ділами Закону; людина виправдовується тільки через віру в Ісуса {{christos:Христа|Месію}}. Тож і ми увірували в {{christos:Христа|Месію}} Ісуса, щоб бути виправданими вірою в {{christos:Христа|Месію}}, а не ділами Закону, бо ділами Закону не виправдається жодна людина.
uk.R: Ми самі народилися юдеями. Ми не неюдеї, яких юдеї називають грішниками. \v 16 Але ми знаємо, що Бог не виправдовує людину за те, що вона виконує вимоги Закону. Бог виправдовує людей тільки через віру в Ісуса {{christos:Христа|Месію}}. Тож і ми повірили в {{christos:Христа|Месію}} Ісуса. Ми зробили це, щоб Бог виправдав нас через віру в {{christos:Христа|Месію}}, а не за виконання вимог Закону. Бо жодну людину Бог не виправдає за виконання вимог Закону.

decisions.choice: Gentile sinners: the Jewish way of speaking of Gentiles as outside God's law
decisions.reason: For Jews, Gentiles were "sinners" because they lived without the law God gave Israel. Paul takes up that way of speaking in order to turn it: even Jews, with all their advantages, must be justified by faith (verse 16), and in verse 17 the label falls on Jewish believers too.

decisions.choice: justified: God declares a person to be in the right before him, acquitted and accepted
alternatives: counted as a faithful member of the covenant only
decisions.reason: δικαιόω is a law-court word: to pronounce someone in the right. Paul uses it of God's verdict on a person, acquitting and accepting them (Romans 3:24-26; 8:33). Verse 17 adds that it happens "in Christ", and 2:21 and 3:6 tie it to righteousness counted to the believer.

decisions.choice: works of the law: doing what the law of Moses requires, as the ground of being accepted by God
alternatives: only the marks of Jewish identity, such as circumcision and food laws
decisions.reason: ἔργων νόμου means acts done in obedience to the law given through Moses. At Antioch the issue was food laws, and in Galatia circumcision, so those are in view; but Paul's argument goes on to the whole law (3:10-12; 5:3). His point is that keeping the law is not what puts anyone right with God.

decisions.choice: through faith in Jesus Christ
alternatives: through the faithfulness of Jesus Christ
decisions.reason: With a person's name after it, πίστις can mean faith that person has or faith directed to that person. Read the first way, Paul means Christ's own faithfulness to God, shown in his death (verse 20; Philippians 2:8), and "we have believed in Christ Jesus" is the believer's answer. Read the second way, he means the believer's faith in Christ. For "faith in Christ": the middle of the verse says just that, "we have believed in Christ Jesus", and in 3:6-9 Paul speaks of believers having faith as Abraham did. For "faithfulness of Christ": the verse would otherwise say the same thing three times, and Paul writes of "the faith of Abraham" for Abraham's own faith (Romans 4:16) and of "the faithfulness of God" (Romans 3:3). Both readings agree that justification comes from Christ and not from the law. We follow the first and give the second in a footnote.

decisions.choice: but only through faith: faith alone is the way, not faith added to works of the law
alternatives: unless also through faith, as if works and faith together justify
decisions.reason: ἐὰν μὴ normally means "except". Taken on its own it might suggest works of the law justify when joined with faith, but the rest of the verse sets faith against works three times: "by faith in Christ and not by works of the law".

decisions.choice: an echo of Psalm 143:2: no living person is righteous before God
decisions.reason: Psalm 143:2 prays that God would not enter into judgment with his servant, for no one living is righteous before him. Paul echoes the psalm and adds "by works of the law": the psalm already said that no one can stand before God on their own record. Romans 3:20 makes the same use of the psalm.

decisions.choice: all flesh: every human being
decisions.reason: πᾶσα σάρξ ("all flesh") is a common Hebrew way of saying all people, mortal and weak (Genesis 6:12; Isaiah 40:5). Here σάρξ does not carry the sense of the sinful self it has in chapter 5.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting.

decisions.choice: justified (L, B); put right with God (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "justify", the word that links this verse to the rest of Paul's letters. Readable says plainly what it means (m2).

decisions.choice: works of [the] law (L); works of the law (B); doing what the law commands (R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the article the Greek leaves out. Balanced keeps Paul's phrase, which recurs in chapter 3. Readable says what the phrase means (m3).

decisions.choice: no flesh (L); no human being (B); no one (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the word "flesh". Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the Hebrew expression (m7), since "flesh" here would suggest the body or the sinful self.

decisions.choice: Gentiles, the people Jews call sinners
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that "sinners" is the Jewish label for Gentiles, not Paul's own judgment of them (m1).

decisions.choice: a person is justified only through faith
decisions.reason: Balanced states the positive side as its own clause, so that "except" is not misread (m5).

decisions.choice: justificar (L, B); Dios declara justo (R)
decisions.reason: The verb first appears in Galatians here. As in Romans, Literal and Balanced keep "justificar", so the term can be followed through the letter, and Readable says what the verdict is, "declarar justo", as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: obras de [la] ley (L); las obras de la ley (B); hacer lo que manda la ley (R); fe en
decisions.reason: Paul's phrase recurs through chapter 3, so Literal and Balanced keep "obras de la ley" every time; Readable says what it means. "Fe en" follows the reading chosen in the meaning decision.

decisions.choice: kuhesabiwa haki (all levels); na Mungu added (R)
decisions.reason: The verb first appears in Galatians here. As in Romans, "kuhesabiwa haki" (to be counted righteous) says it is a verdict and is kept at every level; Readable adds "na Mungu" to say whose verdict it is.

decisions.choice: matendo ya sheria (L, B); kutenda yale ambayo sheria inaamuru (R); imani katika
decisions.reason: "Matendo" (deeds) rather than "kazi" (work, labour), which could suggest a job. "Imani katika" (faith in) follows the reading chosen in the meaning decision; "imani ya" would leave it open but sounds like Christ's own faith.

decisions.choice: justifier (L, B); être déclaré juste par Dieu (R) (for the whole letter)
alternatives: être mis en règle avec Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "justifier", the word that ties this verse to the rest of Paul's letters. Readable says what it means: God's verdict that a person is in the right before him (m2). "Rendre juste" would suggest a change of character rather than a verdict.

decisions.choice: la Loi, with a capital, for the law of Moses; les œuvres de la Loi (L, B); faire ce que la Loi ordonne (R) (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Hebrews and the French style guide, the capital marks the law given through Moses (m3). A law in general (3:21, 5:23) and "the law of Christ" (6:2) are written without it. Readable says what "works of the law" means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: un {{gender:être humain|homme}} (L); personne (B, R), with no span
decisions.reason: The word means any human being. Literal keeps the noun and so carries the setting; Balanced and Readable say "personne", which is already inclusive, and "aucun être humain" needs no setting since it has no traditional alternative here.

decisions.choice: "의롭다고 인정하다 / 인정받다" at every level, Readable adding "하나님께" (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: As in Romans: the verb is God's verdict, declaring a person in the right and accepting them (the meaning decision). "의롭다고 인정하다" says that it is a verdict and keeps the root "의" that ties it to righteousness (2:21; 3:6, 3:21); "의롭다 하심을 받다" is older church language, and "의롭게 되다" would suggest a change of character. Readable keeps the same words and adds "하나님께", where the English Readable says "put right with God".

decisions.choice: "율법의 행위들" (L); "율법의 행위" (B); "율법이 명령하는 것을 행함" (R); "율법" for the law of Moses through the letter
decisions.reason: "율법" names the law God gave Israel through Moses, as in Romans and in the Korean of John. "율법의 행위" (the deeds of the law) is the plain phrase for doing what it requires (the meaning decision); Readable says it as an action, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "예수 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}를 믿는 믿음" at every level
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as faith with Jesus Christ as its object, with his own faithfulness as the other reading. Korean "...의 믿음" would be read as Jesus' own faith, so every level says "...를 믿는 믿음", as in Romans 3:22.

decisions.choice: "어떤 육체도" (L); "아무도" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Flesh" here means a human being (the meaning decision). Literal keeps the word, as in Romans 3:20; Balanced and Readable say "no one".

decisions.choice: "được xưng công chính" (L, B); "được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính" (R) for this verb (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The verb is God's verdict that declares a person in the right (m2). The words are those of the Vietnamese Romans (2:13), which keep it in one family with "sự công chính" (righteousness, 2:21; 3:6); "làm cho công chính" would suggest a change of character rather than a verdict. Readable says who gives the verdict, as the English Readable says "put right with God".

decisions.choice: "những việc làm của luật pháp" (L); "làm những việc luật pháp đòi hỏi" (B); "làm theo những gì luật pháp truyền dạy" (R); "luật pháp", lowercase, for the law of Moses (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The phrase means doing what the law of Moses requires (m3); the forms are those of the Vietnamese Romans (3:20). "Việc làm" is a deed done; "công việc" would suggest a job.

decisions.choice: "đức tin nơi Đức Giê-xu {{christos:Christ|Mê-si-a}}"; "tin vào" for the verb; "đức tin" for pistis at every level (for the whole letter)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the phrase as faith that has Jesus as its object (m4). "Đức tin của" would be heard as the faith Jesus has, so every level says "nơi", as the Vietnamese Romans does (3:22). "Đức tin" is the key term and keeps the noun and the verb "tin" visibly one family.

decisions.choice: "không có xác thịt nào" (L)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "flesh" with "xác thịt", the word kept for sarx, as the Vietnamese Romans does (3:20); here it means no human being (m7), which Balanced and Readable say.

decisions.choice: justificar (L); declarar justo (B); ser aceito por Deus como justo (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Romans and docs/portuguese-style.md section 6. Literal keeps "justificar", the word that ties the letter to Romans; Balanced says "declarar justo", the verdict of m2; Readable, where the English says "put right with God", says "ser aceito por Deus como justo", which keeps the word "justo" and its link with "a justiça" (2:21).

decisions.choice: obras da Lei (L, B); fazer o que a Lei manda (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as in Romans: "obras da Lei" keeps Paul's phrase (m3), with "Lei" capitalised for the Law of Moses at every level; Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does. "Boas obras" would change the sense.

decisions.choice: nenhuma carne (L); nenhum ser humano (B); ninguém (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "carne" in the Hebrew phrase for every mortal (m7); Balanced and Readable give its sense, as the English does.

decisions.choice: መጽደቅ (to be justified, L, B); ከእግዚአብሔር ጋር ትክክለኛ ግንኙነት ማግኘት (to come into a right relationship with God, R), here and through the letter
alternatives: ጻድቅ ተብሎ መቆጠር (to be counted righteous) at every level
decisions.reason: Paul's verb means that God declares a person in the right before him and accepts them (meaning decision m2). "መጽደቅ" is the word of the same root as "ጽድቅ" (righteousness), as in Romans, and keeps the two together; Readable says what it means in plain words, as the English Readable says "put right with God".

decisions.choice: የሕግ ሥራ (works of the law), here and through the letter; ሕጉ የሚለውን ማድረግ (R)
decisions.reason: Paul's phrase means doing what the law of Moses requires (meaning decision m3). As in Romans, Amharic keeps it as one fixed phrase, the singular "ሥራ" standing for deeds in general, so a reader can recognise it each time it returns in chapter 3.

decisions.choice: "धर्मी ठहराना" (L, B); "परमेश्वर की दृष्टि में सही ठहराना" (R)
decisions.reason: The key term of Romans for justify: God declares a person in the right before him (meaning decision m2). Literal and Balanced keep the word that links this verse to Paul's other letters; Readable says plainly what it means. The same through this letter.

decisions.choice: "व्यवस्था के काम" (L, B); "व्यवस्था जो कहती है, वह करना" (R)
decisions.reason: As in Romans: "काम", never "कर्म", which carries the idea of karma. Readable says what the phrase means (meaning decision m3), as Romans 3:20 does.

decisions.choice: "कोई भी शरीरधारी" (L); "कोई भी मनुष्य" (B); "कोई भी" (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "flesh" in the form of Romans 3:20; Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the Hebrew expression, every human being (meaning decision m7).

decisions.choice: оправдать at every level
decisions.reason: Key term settled in Romans: "оправдать" at every level, so this verse links with Romans 3:20-28. Readable adds "перед Богом" where the English Readable says "put right with God" (m2).

decisions.choice: дела Закона (L, B); делать то, что говорит Закон (R)
decisions.reason: Key term as in Romans 3:20: the law of Moses is "Закон" with a capital (m3); Russian has no article, so Literal needs no bracket.

decisions.choice: никакая плоть
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "flesh" (m7), as Romans 3:20 does; Balanced and Readable say "никто".

decisions.choice: "義とされる" (L, B), "神に正しい者と認められる" (R); "律法の行い" (L, B), "律法の命じることを行う" (R)
decisions.reason: Settled for Galatians as in Romans 3:20 and 3:28: God declares a person in the right and accepts them (m2), and works of the law are doing what the law of Moses requires (m3). The same forms hold through chapters 3 and 5.

decisions.choice: "イエス・キリストへの信仰" (L, B); "イエス・キリストを信じる信仰" (R)
alternatives: "イエス・キリストの信仰", keeping the bare genitive
decisions.reason: The meaning decisions read faith in Jesus Christ (m4, with a footnote on the other reading). Japanese "への" says this plainly, as in Romans 3:22; the same holds for 2:20 and 3:22.

decisions.choice: виправдати (every level)
alternatives: поставити в правильні стосунки з Богом
decisions.reason: The style guide and Romans keep "виправдати" at every level for God's verdict that a person is in the right before him (m2); where the English Readable says "put right with God", Ukrainian Readable says that God justifies, which reads plainly. Book-wide, with "праведність" for righteousness.

decisions.choice: діла Закону (L, B); виконувати вимоги Закону (R)
decisions.reason: As Romans: "Закон" with a capital for the law of Moses (m3), and "діла Закону" at Literal and Balanced; Readable says what the works are, as the English does. Book-wide, with "язичники" (L, B) and "неюдеї" (R) for the Gentiles, and "тіло" (L, B) for sarx.

source.text: εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος;

records.literal_gloss: If but seeking to be justified in Christ we were found also ourselves sinners, [is] then Christ of sin a servant?

en.L: But if, while seeking to be justified in {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, we ourselves also were found [to be] sinners, [is] {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} then a servant of sin?
en.B: But if, while we seek to be justified in {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}, we ourselves are found to be sinners too, does that make {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} a servant of sin?
en.R: We are trying to be put right with God by being joined to {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}. Suppose this shows that we too are sinners, just like the Gentiles. Does that mean {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} is working for sin?

es.L: Pero si, buscando ser justificados en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, también nosotros mismos fuimos hallados pecadores, ¿es entonces {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} servidor del pecado?
es.B: Pero si, mientras buscamos ser justificados en {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}, resulta que también nosotros somos pecadores, ¿hace eso {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} un servidor del pecado?
es.R: Buscamos que Dios nos declare justos por estar unidos {{christos:a Cristo|al Mesías}}. Supongamos que esto muestra que también nosotros somos pecadores, igual que los gentiles. ¿Quiere decir eso que {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}} trabaja para el pecado?

sw.L: Lakini ikiwa, tukitafuta kuhesabiwa haki katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sisi wenyewe pia tumeonekana kuwa wenye dhambi, je, basi {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} ni mtumishi wa dhambi?
sw.B: Lakini ikiwa, tunapotafuta kuhesabiwa haki katika {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, sisi wenyewe tunaonekana kuwa wenye dhambi pia, je, hiyo inamfanya {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} kuwa mtumishi wa dhambi?
sw.R: Tunatafuta kuhesabiwa haki na Mungu kwa kuunganishwa na {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}. Tuseme jambo hili linaonyesha kwamba sisi nasi ni wenye dhambi, sawa na watu wa mataifa. Je, hiyo inamaanisha kwamba {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anaifanyia kazi dhambi?

fr.L: Mais si, en cherchant à être justifiés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, nous avons nous-mêmes aussi été trouvés pécheurs, {{christos:Christ|le Messie}} [est-il] donc serviteur du péché ?
fr.B: Mais si, alors que nous cherchons à être justifiés {{christos:en Christ|dans le Messie}}, il se trouve que nous sommes, nous aussi, des pécheurs, le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} serait-il donc au service du péché ?
fr.R: Nous cherchons à être déclarés justes par Dieu en étant unis au {{christos:Christ|Messie}}. Imaginons que cela montre que nous sommes, nous aussi, des pécheurs, exactement comme les non-Juifs. Est-ce que cela veut dire que le {{christos:Christ|Messie}} travaille pour le péché ?

ko.L: 그러나 만일 우리가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에서 의롭다고 인정받기를 구하다가 우리 자신도 죄인으로 드러났다면, 그러면 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죄의 일꾼이십니까?
ko.B: 그런데 우리가 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}} 안에서 의롭다고 인정받으려고 하다가 우리 자신도 죄인으로 드러난다면, {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죄를 섬기는 분이 되신다는 말입니까?
ko.R: 우리는 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}와 하나가 됨으로써 하나님께 의롭다고 인정받으려고 합니다. 그런데 이 일 때문에 우리도 유대인이 아닌 사람들과 똑같이 죄인이라는 것이 드러났다고 해 봅시다. 그렇다면 {{christos:그리스도|메시아}}께서 죄를 위해 일하신다는 말입니까?

vi.L: Nhưng nếu trong khi tìm cách được xưng công chính trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, chính chúng ta cũng bị thấy là tội nhân, thì {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là người phục vụ tội lỗi sao?
vi.B: Nhưng nếu trong khi tìm cách được xưng công chính trong {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}, chính chúng ta cũng bị xem là tội nhân, thì phải chăng {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} là người phục vụ tội lỗi?
vi.R: Chúng ta đang tìm cách để được Đức Chúa Trời công nhận là công chính bằng cách hiệp nhất với {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}}. Giả sử điều đó cho thấy chính chúng ta cũng là tội nhân, giống như dân ngoại. Vậy có phải {{christos:Đấng Christ|Đấng Mê-si-a}} đang làm việc cho tội lỗi không?
